programs.name: unisam2
programs.purpose: Resample a two-dimensional array of floats onto a uniform grid using linear or cubic interpolation.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: UNISAM2 - UNIformly SAMple a 2-D function f(x1,x2)

params.name: x1
params.description: Input coordinates in the first dimension; when supplied, their count determines nx1 and nx1, dx1, and fx1 are not read.

params.name: nx1
params.description: Number of input samples in the first dimension when x1 is absent.

params.name: dx1
params.description: Input coordinate interval in the first dimension when x1 is absent.

params.name: fx1
params.description: First input coordinate in the first dimension when x1 is absent.

params.name: n1
params.description: Number of output samples in the first dimension.

params.name: d1
params.description: Output coordinate interval in the first dimension.

params.name: f1
params.description: First output coordinate in the first dimension.

params.name: x2
params.description: Input coordinates in the second dimension; when supplied, their count determines nx2 and nx2, dx2, and fx2 are not read.

params.name: nx2
params.description: Number of input samples in the second dimension when x2 is absent.

params.name: dx2
params.description: Input coordinate interval in the second dimension when x2 is absent.

params.name: fx2
params.description: First input coordinate in the second dimension when x2 is absent.

params.name: n2
params.description: Number of output samples in the second dimension.

params.name: d2
params.description: Output coordinate interval in the second dimension.

params.name: f2
params.description: First output coordinate in the second dimension.

params.name: method1
params.description: Interpolation method selected by its first character: linear, mono, akima, or spline. The code applies this method along the second dimension.

params.name: method2
params.description: Interpolation method selected by its first character: linear, mono, akima, or spline. The code applies this method along the first dimension.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Interpolation is performed first along dimension 2 and then dimension 1, using float coordinates and library linear or cubic interpolation. Arithmetic order and the cubic coefficient calculations affect bitwise results. The method parameter names are applied to the opposite dimensions from their numbering.
programs.difficulty_reason: The program buffers a two-dimensional array and supports four interpolation methods in each pass.

test_cases.description: Resample a regular input grid with linear interpolation.
test_cases.command: suspike nt=8 ntr=4 nspk=2 ix1=1 it1=2 ix2=4 it2=7 | sustrip outpar=/dev/null | unisam2 nx1=8 nx2=4 n1=12 n2=6 method1=linear method2=linear > out.bin

test_cases.description: Exercise irregular coordinates and monotonic and Akima interpolation.
test_cases.command: suspike nt=4 ntr=4 nspk=2 ix1=1 it1=2 ix2=4 it2=3 | sustrip outpar=/dev/null | unisam2 x1=0,1,3,6 x2=0,2,3,7 n1=7 n2=6 method1=mono method2=akima > out.bin

test_cases.description: Exercise spline interpolation and explicit output coordinates.
test_cases.command: suspike nt=4 ntr=4 nspk=2 ix1=1 it1=1 ix2=4 it2=4 | sustrip outpar=/dev/null | unisam2 nx1=4 nx2=4 n1=5 d1=0.5 f1=0 n2=5 d2=0.5 f2=0 method1=spline method2=spline > out.bin

programs.name: xy2z
programs.purpose: Convert binary float coordinate pairs into spikes on a uniformly scaled two-dimensional float grid.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: XY2Z - converts (X,Y)-pairs to spike Z values on a uniform grid

params.name: npairs
params.description: Number of binary float pairs to read.

params.name: scale
params.description: Value assigned to grid cells containing pairs.

params.name: nx1
params.description: Size of the fast output dimension.

params.name: nx2
params.description: Size of the slow output dimension.

params.name: x1pad
params.description: Padding used when scaling coordinates in the fast dimension.

params.name: x2pad
params.description: Padding used when scaling coordinates in the slow dimension.

params.name: yx
params.description: When nonzero, the first float is assigned to x1 and the second to x2; when zero, the assignments are reversed.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Coordinates are scaled with float arithmetic and rounded with NINT; rounding near cell boundaries can change the selected cell. A zero coordinate range causes division by zero, and insufficient or unsuitable padding can permit out-of-bounds indices. Repeated pairs overwrite rather than accumulate.
programs.difficulty_reason: The program buffers coordinate pairs and a two-dimensional grid and scales and rounds coordinates into grid indices.

test_cases.description: Grid four pairs with the default coordinate ordering.
test_cases.command: suspike nt=8 ntr=1 nspk=2 ix1=1 it1=1 ix2=1 it2=4 | sustrip outpar=/dev/null | xy2z npairs=4 nx1=8 nx2=8 x1pad=2 x2pad=2 scale=1 yx=0 > out.bin

test_cases.description: Reverse coordinate assignments and use a different spike value and padding.
test_cases.command: suspike nt=8 ntr=1 nspk=2 ix1=1 it1=1 ix2=1 it2=4 | sustrip outpar=/dev/null | xy2z npairs=4 nx1=10 nx2=12 x1pad=1 x2pad=3 scale=2.5 yx=1 > out.bin

programs.name: z2xyz
programs.purpose: Convert a binary float grid into ASCII triples containing row index, column index, and value.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: Z2XYZ - convert binary floats representing Z-values to ascii

params.name: n1
params.description: Number of floats in each input row.

params.name: outpar
params.description: File to receive the number of input rows as n2.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Values are formatted with printf using %11.4e, so textual rounding and locale can affect output. The error path formats a size_t argument with %d, which is undefined behavior.
programs.difficulty_reason: The program reads one row of floats at a time and formats each value with its indices.

test_cases.description: Convert a small stripped spike panel to ASCII triples.
test_cases.command: suspike nt=8 ntr=4 nspk=2 ix1=1 it1=2 ix2=4 it2=7 | sustrip outpar=/dev/null | z2xyz n1=8 outpar=/dev/null > out.txt

test_cases.description: Interpret the same kind of float stream using shorter output rows.
test_cases.command: suspike nt=8 ntr=2 nspk=1 ix1=1 it1=3 | sustrip outpar=/dev/null | z2xyz n1=4 outpar=/dev/null > out.txt

programs.license_note: The credits say the program is based on b2a by Jack Cohen.
